_comment: Canonical defect register — closure criterion G2.3 (`docs/PROJECT-CLOSURE-GATE.md` §5, owner ruling 6). Repository-local and version-controlled on purpose: GitHub Issues are explicitly NOT canonical, because closure must not depend on an external tracker being reachable. Issues may mirror this file. PASS = zero OPEN P0/P1 rows. Read it with `aisef.control.defects:read` — the same reader the closure probe uses, so a report and the gate cannot disagree. This file is missing = UNRUNNABLE at closure; this file present with an empty `defects` = a real PASS.
_boundary: `docs/FAILURE-TAXONOMY.md` answers *what went wrong and what did we learn* (133 closed rows: symptom, root cause, lesson, fix). This register answers *what is outstanding now, at what severity*. A defect sits here while open and there once understood, and a row here points at its taxonomy row by id instead of restating it — nothing is copied in either direction. Work that is wanted but whose absence is not a wrong result (the POST_CLOSE list in the contract's §7, `docs/ROADMAP-POST-1.0.md`) is not a defect and is not entered here.
_fields: id (stable, never reused) · severity (P0–P3, scale below) · status (OPEN | CLOSED) · title · introduced / fixed (version or commit, where known; empty when it is not) · evidence (the regression test, or the command that recomputes the measurement) · check (optional: the `gate.CHECK_NAMES` entry the defect bears on) · taxonomy (optional: the FAILURE-TAXONOMY.md row id) · notes. No timestamps: the file must digest the same on every read or G2.3's staleness detection reads noise as change.

severity_scale._comment: Reused by reference, never redefined here. P0 = cannot install, data loss, security issue, incorrect gate result. P1 = cannot complete the lifecycle without author assistance. P2 = significant confusion / DX friction. P3 = cosmetic or optional. The reader refuses a register that names another source or edits `blocking`.

defects.title: A test run with no readable results records other stories' requirements as regressions
defects.evidence: python3 validation/o3_preservation_radius.py → `todo: 4 scored stories, 36 behaviours, 2 confirmed regressors, 4 uncorroborated REOPENED` (FR-1, FR-2, FR-4 owned by STORY-02-01 and FR-9 by STORY-01-02, all flipped by STORY-02-02 at at=1788947583.932249, an event whose `test` tool_run is ok=True exit_code=0 with `test_format: ""`, `test_ids: []`, `failed_ids: []`). No regression test yet.
defects.notes:
Same class as taxonomy row 155 (absence read as regression), in the branch that fix did not cover: `ledger._observe_tests`, when `readable` is false, calls `rollup(line, False, why)` for the home story, so every requirement that story `covers` — owned by earlier, VERIFIED stories — is observed not-green and `observe` records REOPENED. Nothing red was read anywhere. P1 and not P2 because the loop's own arithmetic is corrupted by it (`improve` stops on Δverified − Δreopened) and only a human comparing the ledger against the evidence can tell the artifact from a regression; P1 and not P0 because no gate verdict is demonstrably wrong on disk — the mechanism by which one could be (a behaviour REOPENED by another story is dropped from that story's `preservation` list, `complexity.verified_touched`) is real but was never reached here: STORY-02-02 was the last story of that corpus and it failed. The trigger is not exotic — any project whose test output AISEF cannot parse yields `test_format: ""`. false_pass=false: false FAIL, not false PASS: an unreadable test run marks other stories' requirements REOPENED — it invents a regression, it does not pass a defect. Lives in the ledger projection, not in a gate check.
CLOSED 2026-09-14. The fix is the removal of one call: `rollup(line, False, why)` in the `not readable` branch of `ledger._observe_tests`. The per-criterion `note()`s stay -- not reading a test name genuinely means this story has proven nothing, and `gap_kind` classifies those as UNTRACED. What is gone is flipping OTHER stories' requirements: a requirement is a shared cross-story artifact and must not change status because one run could not be read.
No false-PASS risk, and this is the reason the fix is safe rather than merely small: an unreadable run only ever passed `False`, so removing the call can prevent a false REOPENED and cannot produce a VERIFIED.
Measured before and after on the four todo* corpora with `python3 validation/o3_preservation_radius.py`: `todo` goes from 4 uncorroborated REOPENED to 0, the other three were already 0, and the confirmed-regressor counts are unchanged (todo-oc 4, todo-cli 5, todo 2, todo-e2e 4; 15 of 32 stories). Real regression detection is therefore intact -- the negative control is in `tests/test_ledger.py::TestKhongDocDuocKhongPhaiHoiQuy::test_mot_phep_thu_do_that_van_lam_reopened`.
taxonomy stays 155: this is the same failure class (absence read as regression) in a branch that fix did not cover, and the register's rule is to point at a taxonomy row, never to restate or duplicate it.

defects.title: A blocking gate decision can rest on the model reviewer alone
defects.evidence: python3 bin/aisef closure -> G2.4b: 17 of 122 blocks judge-alone (13.9 %), all four properties hold; closure-evidence/judge-only-audit.json (2026-09-14) carries the per-property assertions. SUPERSEDED FIGURE: this row previously quoted 36.8 % (21 of 57) from `aisef.control.reviewer_qual` over the four todo* corpora. That measurement predates defect 158, which took the blocking-line parse rate from 0/177 to 116/177 -- `Finding.id` could not be computed on real reviewer output at all when it was taken. The old number is kept here in words, not deleted, because the published O1 report still carries it and docs/O1-RECOMPUTE-AFTER-158.md is the dated addendum that reconciles them. Lifecycle effect, same corpus: todo-e2e STORY-... ended `failed` on the judge's word with no deterministic check disagreeing.
defects.notes:
Closure criterion G2.4b owns the verdict on this fact (REQUIRED_WITH_WAIVER_ALLOWED, owner ruling 1: no reviewer redesign for closure's sake, and the measured rate stays a published property).
P1 -> P2 on 2026-09-14. The P1 rested on one argument: that the contract's exemption for the model-judge error rate is conditional on 'no blocking decision rests on the judge alone', and that condition does not hold. Owner ruling 1 REPLACED that blanket condition with four named properties -- a judge-only block must be explicitly identifiable in evidence, distinguishable from deterministic blocking, have a human escape/override path, and be unable to masquerade as a deterministic guarantee. G2.4b now PASSES on exactly those four, without a waiver, so the owner's stated test is met and the P1's own justification is superseded by the ruling it was written under. This row's earlier note anticipated the reading ('the argument for P2 is owner ruling 1 read as also excusing it from G2.3'); the ruling settled it.
NOT closed: judge-alone blocks still exist (17 of 122) and the rate remains a published property of the framework, so the fact stays on the register. P2 is the honest severity for a measured property that blocks nothing and sets no gate -- it does not gate G2.3, and it is not being waived, which are different things.
false_pass=false throughout: a judge-only block is a blocking decision resting on a model-judge check, not a deterministic or structural check passing when it should fail.

defects.title: `_analyze.cut_sessions` merges two bench cohorts on the three tasks they share
defects.evidence: tests/bench/_analyze.py: `_DUONG_DAN_PHIEN = re.compile(r"\.bench[\w.-]*/run/([\w-]+)/([\w-]+)/a(\d+)")` matches any ledger directory but captures only (condition, task, attempt), so `.bench/run/…` and `.bench-c1b/run/…` land on one key. Recorded in docs/BENCH-TASK-DISCRIMINATION.md §6 with the three affected tasks (`sec-1`, `sec-2`, `state-3`).
defects.notes: Deliberately not fixed: both published bench reports quote this function's output, so re-keying it makes a re-run of `analyze` print a table that differs from the printed evidence. P2 — the wrong number is an auxiliary cut-session count in a bench analysis helper, it blocks nothing and sets no gate. The contract lists it POST_CLOSE (§7); that is a scheduling statement, and P2 is the severity — they agree, and neither is derived from the other. false_pass=false: a bench analysis counter, not a gate check at all.

defects.title: criterion identity is positional, so a test can silently become proof for a different criterion
defects.introduced: pre-dates this wave; surfaced 2026-09-14 by the marks-cli closure corpus
defects.evidence: marks-cli _bmad-output/plan-reconciliation.json §incomplete_withdrawal.how_the_agent_resolved_it; tests named AC-STORY-01-02-1 in marks-cli tests/dispatch.test.js now assert STORY-02-02 `list` behaviour while that code maps to 'unknown verb exits 1'; AC-STORY-01-02-4 is orphaned
defects.notes:
false_pass=true: `criteria have tests` is a blocking STRUCTURAL check and a shifted test satisfies it while proving another behaviour. First registered true false PASS, so G2.4a moved PASSED -> FAILED; owner decision 2026-09-14 was that it stays FAILED until fixed, not waived and not weakened. Not preventable by instruction: the developer never sees the criterion list, so the fix had to be a detector plus a stable identity, not a convention.
CLOSED 2026-09-14 in two commits, against the owner's five acceptance points:
  (1) delete/reorder cannot silently change identity — identity is now the pair (code, content digest); `acceptance.drift()` names the codes whose criterion text moved. Reorder is the case a count cannot see: same count, nothing orphaned, each test proving the other's criterion.
  (2) a test cannot silently become proof for another criterion — same digest pair; for a story already merged DONE, `run._done_criteria_drift` compares the recorded contract note against today's criteria and the epic STOPS instead of skipping it silently. Re-running cannot repair that case: the work is on the main branch, so the developer would open an already-green tree (bug 143's measured failure).
  (3) orphaned AC ids detected — `acceptance.orphans()`, blocking in the gate.
  (4) duplicate/mismatched mappings detected — `acceptance.overloaded()` blocks a test whose name carries two codes of one story (two criteria, one behaviour: no count sees it, `missing` is empty and nothing is orphaned). Separately, the register's `check_kind` is now DERIVED from `gate.CHECK_KIND` and a hand-written kind that contradicts the framework reads UNRUNNABLE — declaring a structural false PASS as `model-judge` was itself a way past G2.4a.
  (5) the gate cannot PASS `criteria have tests` on drifted identity — orphans and ambiguous mappings block there; drift is caught at plan level because within one attempt the criteria and the note are the same text by construction, so a drift comparison inside `evaluate()` could never fire.
No baseline reads as CANNOT DECIDE, never as fine — merging those two is the same false-PASS class. The note is therefore also written when an existing one lacks the digest map, so corpora that already have work to lose acquire a baseline.
Corpus status: the identity sweep over all 7 marks-cli stories finds exactly one residual problem, STORY-01-02's orphaned AC-STORY-01-02-4 — a present-state defect the replay cannot see, because ADR-005 V4 replays with the acceptance count recorded at that attempt (4), which was correct then. G4 evidence stays not-closure-valid until that orphan is resolved, at 7/7 or not.

defects.title: a 401 names the credential source but not the client and model that failed
defects.introduced: pre-dates this wave; surfaced 2026-09-14 by a misdiagnosis in this repository
defects.evidence: marks-cli _bmad-output/evidence/STORY-04-01.jsonl: six agent_run records carry client=opencode model=9router/mycombo session_id=ses_*; the failing record carries client=claude model=claude-opus-5[1m] session_id=<uuid> exit_status=auth. The error string named ANTHROPIC_API_KEY and nothing else, and was read as 'the project's key rotated' -- on a project whose ~/.config/opencode/opencode.json sets disabled_providers: ["anthropic"]. Probed after the fix: GET /v1/models -> 200, POST /v1/chat/completions model=mycombo -> 200 resolving downstream to MiniMax-M3.
defects.notes:
auth_hint listed whichever AUTH_ENV_NAMES were present in the child environment and asserted they were used. Presence in the shell is not evidence of use. It was only called from claude_code.py, so the sentence was true of the session it described -- but it described the credential SOURCE, not the PATH, and on a project with more than one client configured only the client and model attribute a 401 to a request. The opencode adapter had no auth branch at all, so a genuine 9router rejection produced a bare line the operator could not act on.
Fixed: auth_hint takes client and model and names them first; environment variables are named only for clients that actually read them (ENV_AUTH_CLIENTS), so an opencode failure never points at an Anthropic variable the request never touched; the opencode adapter now produces the message too. The hint also says that a wrong --client is a likelier cause than a rotated key, which is what actually happened.
Severity P2: it sets no gate and passes no check -- it cost a wrong diagnosis and a wasted report, not a wrong verdict.

defects.title: a credential rejection is charged against the story's quality attempts
defects.introduced: pre-dates this wave; surfaced 2026-09-14 on the marks-cli corpus
defects.evidence: marks-cli run.log 2026-09-14 12:58:44: `attempt=1 FAIL ... attempt=2 START` on a 401 whose session note records moved_tree: false and 'auth and the tree is untouched -- nothing to grade'. quality_attempts counts attempts where not a.infra, and `auth` is not in INFRA_STATUSES, so the story spent quality budget on a session the agent had no part in.
defects.notes:
`auth` is kept OUT of INFRA_STATUSES deliberately and that reasoning is sound and measured: a rejected credential is not transient, so retrying spends the infra budget on a failure that repeats identically (2026-09-12: 176 s per attempt, $0, three attempts, nothing learned). The defect is that excluding it did not achieve the stated intent -- it only moved the cost to the QUALITY budget and retried anyway. Classifying a status controls accounting, not whether a retry happens; the comment assumed it controlled both.
Fixed with the idiom already in the same function for 'not the agent's fault AND retrying is pointless', which the isolation branch uses: infra=True (nothing was ever scored, so no quality attempt is charged) plus fatal=True (stop now). `auth` stays out of INFRA_STATUSES, so the measured no-retry finding is preserved.
Same shape as taxonomy row 130, which measured it for max_turns: a story spending its whole budget without ever producing a verdict leaves the next developer no feedback.
